newsitem.title: POLAND: AGROS NEW ISSUE PRICED AT PLN 65-80/SHR.
newsitem.headline: AGROS NEW ISSUE PRICED AT PLN 65-80/SHR.

text.p: The price range for book-building for a public offering of 2.425 million shares of Agros Holding SA food trader and producer was set at 65-80 zlotys per share, the issue's lead manager said on Monday.
"The initial range for the book-building is set at 65-80 zlotys," Pawel Tamborski, the head of the primary market division at Creditanstalt Securities SA, told a news conference.
The offering is scheduled for March 20-26.

Tamborski said the book-building range was set below Agros' recent market price to take into account the dilution of earnings after the new issue but added the final strike price, due to be announced on March 18, could change.
Agros opened on Monday down three percent at 80 zlotys.
Tamborski said Agros was starting on Monday a road show that would take it to London and all major European centres including several Polish cities.

The offering, one of the largest on the Warsaw bourse, is divided into a 1.24 million-share offer for selected institutional investors, a 300,000-share open tranche and a 890,000-share one-for-five rights issue.
Agros president Zofia Gaber, also present, said the company was especially keen to attract large international investment funds with its institutional offer.
"We expect large investment funds with mid-term investment strategies to become investors in the new issue though that doesn't mean that other investors are not welcome," Gaber said.

Tamborski said that on March 18 Creditanstalt would announce the make up of an underwriting consortium but he said he expected it not to differ much from a consortium set up to carry out the share subscription.

He said Agros shares abroad would be offered by a consortium led by Creditanstalt Securities and including Creditanstalt Investment Banking AG, CS First Boston, HSBC, Societe Generale, Robert Fleming and UBS Ltd.
The Polish consortium would include securities units of seven Polish banks.
Agros predicts its group net earnings to grow to 81.3 million zlotys in 1997 and 99.1 million zlotys in 1998 from about 49.0 million in 1996.
It predicts sales rising to 1.55 billion and 2.05 billion respectively from last year's 1.24 billion.
